cards.text: Grab your apron, friend. The Jewish Passover is near, and Jesus goes up to Jerusalem. Fair warning: this is NOT gonna be a quiet trip.
He walks into the temple courts and finds men selling animals, and money changers seated at their tables. It's a livestock auction and a bank lobby. In the SAME room.

cards.question: In the temple courts, men are selling cattle, sheep and ___.

cards.text: Now watch what Jesus does. He doesn't ask to speak to the manager. He takes some cords and makes something out of them.

cards.question: What does Jesus make out of cords in the temple courts?
When Jesus drives everyone out of the temple courts, the sheep and cattle go too.
What does Jesus do to the money changers and their tables?

answers.text: He pours out their coins and overturns the tables
He carries their tables out to the street
He sits down and checks every one of their counts

cards.text: Coins rolling EVERYWHERE. Then Jesus turns to the men selling doves: "Get these out of here!" That is NOT a suggestion, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells the dove sellers they've turned His Father's house into a ___.

cards.text: His disciples are watching all of this, and they remember something that is written in Scripture. Me? Something wild happens and the only thing I remember is that I left the oven on.

cards.question: What is the Scripture the disciples remember about?

cards.text: After all this, the Jews there have a demand for Jesus. And it is NOT "Can we help you pick up the coins?"

cards.question: What do the Jews demand that Jesus show them?

answers.text: A sign to prove His authority
A letter from the high priest
A record of His family line

cards.text: Here's Jesus' answer, and you might want to sit down for this one. Destroy this temple, He says, and He will raise it up again.

cards.question: Jesus says that if they destroy this temple, He will raise it up again in ___ days.
The Jews answer Jesus that this temple took forty-six years to build.

cards.text: Forty-six YEARS. Then they ask Him, "and You are going to raise it up in three days?"
They're picturing the building, stone by stone. But Jesus was speaking about a different temple.

cards.question: What temple was Jesus speaking about?
When do the disciples remember that Jesus said this about the temple?

answers.text: After He was raised from the dead
On the walk back to Galilee
At the very next Passover Feast

cards.text: Then they believe the Scripture and the word Jesus had spoken. Some things take a while to land, and believe me, a stamper who spent years in a junk drawer is the KING of taking a while.
Meanwhile, Jesus is in Jerusalem for the Passover Feast, and He's doing signs. Lots of people are watching.

cards.question: Many people see the signs Jesus is doing and ___ in His name.
Jesus entrusts Himself to the people at the feast who believe in His name.
Why doesn't Jesus entrust Himself to the people at the feast?

cards.text: Nobody has to tell Jesus what people are like, because He knew what was in a man. Me? I can't even tell what's in a cookie box until I open the lid.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He sits down and checks every one of their counts" is noticeably longer than the others and reads as silly next to a scene of overturned tables. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 3 retells Jesus' line but cuts off the ending. Card 4 then asks the baker to fill in that missing wording ("in three days"). The baker is guessing the next words of a line they haven't seen. The blank isn't testing meaning they can reason out from what was told.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This true or false card asks whether the Jews said the temple took forty-six years to build, but no story card has set up their reply yet. The baker has no context and can only get it right by luck. Card 6 then tells the reply afterward and repeats "Forty-six YEARS," so the setup comes after the question when it should come before it.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke compares the disciples' understanding coming later, after the resurrection, with Papa Dorin's years in the junk drawer. The drawer years were about waiting to be remembered, not about slowly understanding something. The two actions don't match, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" comes right after the card about the disciples believing after the resurrection. It suggests v23 happens at the same time as v22. But v22 looks ahead to after the resurrection, and v23 returns to the Passover Feast at the time of the temple clearing. The timeline the card implies is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Several story cards are plain retelling with no Papa Dorin energy, such as stop 2 cards 3, 7 and 11. The jokes that are there are mild, for example stop 1 card 1's "NOT gonna be a quiet trip." Overall the voice reads closer to a pleasant narrator than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
